- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or add downward bias.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.0), model often underestimates; increase forecast slightly or adjust for mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overcorrects and overshoots; cap forecast rise to 2–3% per day.
- Model consistently underestimates true price drops after sentiment shifts to negative; add 1–2% buffer below forecast for downward moves.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture early mean reversion; adjust forecast to reflect 10–15% drop from peak within first 5–7 days if sentiment turns negative.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.0 values, model tends to ignore volatility; increase forecast volatility by 1–2% to reflect market uncertainty.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.0–0.5), model often averages out; use weighted average with higher weight to recent sentiment peaks.
